Title: Aperitivo culture / Camparino in Galleria
Description: Beyond the Navigli: Brera's terraces and the Camparino in Galleria, birthplace of the Milanese spritz-and-snacks ritual.
How to get there: In Milan — Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, Metro Duomo

Title: Bagatti Valsecchi house-museum
Description: A Neo-Renaissance fantasy home crammed with armour, curiosities, secret compartments and hidden plumbing disguised as antiques.
How to get there: In Milan — Montenapoleone, Metro M3 Montenapoleone

Title: Bar Luce at Fondazione Prada
Description: Wes Anderson designed this cafe — pastel terrazzo, jukebox, two custom pinball machines; inside Fondazione Prada with its gold 'Haunted House' tower.
How to get there: In Milan — Metro M3 Lodi T.I.B.B.

Title: Branca Tower
Description: A skeletal 108m steel tower Gio Ponti built in Parco Sempione in ten weeks in 1933; a glass lift shoots you to a tiny belvedere with Alp views.
How to get there: In Milan — Parco Sempione, Metro M1/M2 Cadorna

Title: Brera district + Orto Botanico di Brera
Description: Milan's arty village of cobbled lanes and galleries wrapped around a hidden 18th-century botanical garden with ancient ginkgos.
How to get there: In Milan — Brera, Metro M2/M3 Lanza or Montenapoleone

Title: Brera Pinacoteca
Description: Raphael, Caravaggio and Mantegna's foreshortened dead Christ in one grand gallery; do it only if craving painting.
How to get there: In Milan — Brera, Metro M2/M3 Lanza

Title: Cimitero Monumentale
Description: An open-air museum of Art Nouveau and Symbolist tombs — melting bronze figures, miniature temples, impossible staircases. Free, uncrowded.
How to get there: In Milan — Metro M5 Monumentale

Title: Classic Milanese food crawl
Description: Saffron risotto alla milanese, breaded cotoletta, slow-braised ossobuco, and panettone — Milan invented all four.
How to get there: In Milan — trattorias citywide

Title: Duomo → La Scala kids' treasure hunt
Description: A scavenger hunt through the centre with clues and a prize.
How to get there: In Milan — starts at the Duomo

Title: Duomo + rooftop terraces
Description: Walk up among the spires and flying buttresses with the Alps on the horizon; book a timed rooftop ticket to skip the line.
How to get there: In Milan — Piazza del Duomo, Metro M1/M3 Duomo

Title: Duomo archaeological area + Battistero
Description: Descend beneath the cathedral to the 4th-century baptistery and Roman ruins where Milan was Christianized — eerie underground layer.
How to get there: In Milan — under the Duomo, Metro Duomo; combo ticket

Title: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II + bull-heel spin
Description: The glittering 1877 iron-and-glass arcade; find the mosaic bull on the floor and spin on your heel in the divot for good luck.
How to get there: In Milan — between Duomo and La Scala, Metro Duomo

Title: Gelato + the Galleria
Description: A cone from a good gelateria, the bull-heel spin, and a lap of the glittering arcade — an easy jet-lagged arrival-day win.
How to get there: In Milan — Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, Metro Duomo

Title: Highline Galleria skywalk
Description: A 250m catwalk along the Galleria rooftops, 40m above shoppers, popping out over Piazza del Duomo; reopened Feb 2026, timed tickets.
How to get there: In Milan — Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, Metro Duomo

Title: Leonardo Science Museum + the Toti submarine
Description: Italy's biggest science-and-tech museum: Leonardo's machine models, steam trains, planes, and the walk-through Enrico Toti submarine.
How to get there: In Milan — ~30 min by metro from the flat

Title: Museo di Storia Naturale — mineral & gem hall
Description: Cathedral-like natural history museum: minerals and gems, a Spinosaurus snout, a cast of 'Stan' the T-rex, pygmy elephants, taxidermy dioramas.
How to get there: In Milan — metro to Porta Venezia, ~30 min

Title: Museum of Senses
Description: Hands-on illusions and sensory tricks — pure play.
How to get there: In Milan — central

Title: Navigli canals aperitivo
Description: Leonardo helped engineer these canals; now Milan's best evening scene. Rhys's first legal Italian aperitivo — a spritz by the water.
How to get there: In Milan — Naviglio Grande, Metro M2 Porta Genova

Title: Panzerotti at Luini
Description: A tiny takeaway behind the Duomo frying one thing since 1949: the panzerotto, a half-moon of dough pocketing molten mozzarella and tomato.
How to get there: In Milan — behind the Duomo, Metro Duomo

Title: San Bernardino alle Ossa (bone chapel)
Description: A small side chapel walled floor-to-ceiling in human skulls and bones — macabre and beautiful; gauge a sensitive 9-year-old.
How to get there: In Milan — near Piazza Santo Stefano, walkable from Duomo

Title: Sforza Castle + Michelangelo's Rondanini Pieta
Description: A proper brick fortress with battlements and moats, plus Michelangelo's haunting last unfinished Pieta inside; courtyards free.
How to get there: In Milan — Castello Sforzesco, Metro M1 Cairoli

Title: The Last Supper / Cenacolo Vinciano
Description: Leonardo's fading masterpiece seen in a hushed timed 15-minute slot; sells out weeks to months ahead — book the instant dates are firm.
How to get there: In Milan — Santa Maria delle Grazie; metro/tram to Conciliazione or Cadorna

Title: WWII air-raid shelter, Piazza Grandi
Description: Descend into a restored 1936 bomb shelter — 25 rooms that hid up to 450 civilians, walls scrawled with messages; free hour-long guided tour.
How to get there: In Milan — Piazza Grandi, Metro/tram; advance booking required

Title: Bernina Railway from Tirano
Description: Spiral tunnels, viaducts and glaciers on a UNESCO mountain railway into Switzerland.
How to get there: Day-trip — train ~2h30 to Tirano, then the Bernina

Title: Cremona — violin-making workshop
Description: Watch a luthier build a violin by hand in the world capital of violins.
How to get there: Day-trip — train ~1h from Milan

Title: Mottolino Bike Park (Livigno) — the full DH park (2-night trip)
Description: The most American-style park: gondola, jumps, wooden features, downhill school, trails at every level — and open latest, to Sep 27. Serious DH suits the 12/16/18-yo; the 9-yo can do the lift-side blue with the school.
How to get there: Bus Milano Centrale→Livigno ~4h30 — a 2-NIGHT trip out of Milan, not a day-trip.

Title: Museo Alfa Romeo, Arese
Description: The official Alfa Romeo museum on the old factory site: six floors of racing legends, concept cars and engines. Carless via metro + Z120 bus.
How to get there: M1 metro to Rho Fiera, then Z120 bus; ~45-60 min each way

Title: Orrido di Nesso — Lake Como
Description: A gorge and waterfalls carved through the rock beneath the village.
How to get there: Day-trip — train to Como + bus/boat

Title: Rocca di Angera — Lake Maggiore
Description: A huge fortress above the lake, reached by train and boat.
How to get there: Day-trip — train ~1h + ferry

Title: Novara — climb inside the San Gaudenzio dome
Description: Climb inside a 121m dome on masonry walkways. Escher-grade. Open Sundays, age 6+.
How to get there: On the Milan→Turin train day — 10-min walk from Novara station

Title: Aperitivo at Piazza Vittorio Veneto
Description: Turin invented vermouth and the aperitivo ritual — a spritz/vermouth with free nibbles as the arcades light up; Rhys's first legal one.
How to get there: In Turin — Piazza Vittorio Veneto, early evening

Title: Bicerin at Caffe Al Bicerin
Description: Layered espresso, drinking chocolate and cream (don't stir it), invented in Turin and served the same way since 1763.
How to get there: In Turin — Piazza della Consolata

Title: Chocolate-making experience
Description: Turin is Italy's chocolate capital — make your own.
How to get there: In Turin — central

Title: Gianduiotto and the chocolate crawl
Description: Turin invented gianduja; graze historic caffe-cioccolaterie under the arcades for the gold-wrapped gianduiotto, Nutella's ancestor.
How to get there: In Turin — historic chocolatiers under the arcades, citywide

Title: Magic Turin — black and white squares walk
Description: Self-guided walk on Turin's esoteric lore: Piazza Statuto the dark heart, Piazza Castello the light; hunt the symbols and statues.
How to get there: In Turin — self-guided walk, or book a night ghost-walk

Title: MAUTO — National Automobile Museum
Description: One of the world's great car museums, a designed-to-the-hilt hall of a century of automobiles down by the Lingotto.
How to get there: In Turin — Metro toward Lingotto

Title: Mole Antonelliana — glass lift + Cinema Museum
Description: Turin's landmark spire holds Italy's cinema museum plus a glass elevator up through the hollow interior to a terrace 85m over the rooftops.
How to get there: In Turin — ~8-min walk from the flat

Title: Museo Egizio
Description: World's oldest Egyptian museum and most important outside Cairo: mummies, painted sarcophagi, an intact tomb and ~4,000-year-old objects.
How to get there: In Turin — ~10-min walk

Title: Museo Lombroso — criminal anthropology
Description: A genuinely macabre collection — teen-plus.
How to get there: In Turin — central

Title: Museo Regionale di Scienze Naturali
Description: Regional natural science museum with minerals and skeletons; around the corner from the base near the Mole.
How to get there: In Turin — central

Title: Museum of Illusions
Description: Rooms of hands-on optical illusions.
How to get there: In Turin — central

Title: Superga rack railway
Description: An 1884 rack tramway grinds up to the hilltop Basilica of Superga for huge Alpine views and royal tombs; also the 1949 Grande Torino crash site.
How to get there: In Turin — tram 15 to Sassi, then the rack railway

Title: The arcades + Piazza San Carlo
Description: Roughly 18 km of grand covered porticoes strung between baroque squares; drift Via Roma to Piazza San Carlo, Turin's 'drawing room'.
How to get there: In Turin — walk Via Roma through the centre

Title: The Lingotto rooftop test track (Pista 500)
Description: The old Fiat Lingotto factory's banked rooftop test track from the original Italian Job survives as a walkable oval with a hanging bubble.
How to get there: In Turin — Metro to Lingotto

Title: The Pietro Micca tunnels
Description: A 14-km maze of 18th-century military counter-mines; the museum takes you down into the real cramped, dark galleries. Book a guided descent.
How to get there: In Turin — central; book a guided descent

Title: Torino Sotterranea — underground Turin
Description: Guided walk through siege tunnels, cellars and WWII air-raid shelters.
How to get there: In Turin — guided, central meeting point

Title: Damanhur — Temples of Humankind
Description: A hand-dug underground esoteric cathedral of sacred geometry.
How to get there: Best as Mon Sep 14 day-trip — train Turin→Ivrea (~1h) + taxi (~€30); pre-book English tour

Title: Grotta di Bossea
Description: An Alpine karst show-cave for the rockhound.
How to get there: Day-trip — needs bus/car from Mondovì; long

Title: La Mandria park — forest gravel spin
Description: A 15km circular compact-gravel loop through oak forest with wildlife and picnic stops — safe, non-technical off-tarmac a 9-yo can do solo. Tamer than real trail riding.
How to get there: ~12km from Turin centre by local transit/bike path.

Title: Pila Bike Park (Aosta) — kids' park, Sep 11–13 ONLY
Description: The best kids' park found: green/blue family routes, a pump track, and FREE downhill courses for ages 6–12 at two bike schools. But 2026 lifts CLOSE Sun Sep 13 — a hard deadline.
How to get there: Train Turin→Aosta ~2h, then a 5-min walk to the Aosta–Pila gondola — needs an Aosta overnight (sleep there Sep 11 or 12). Verify the Ivrea–Aosta line isn't on bus-replacement.
Cost: ~€146 lifts (kids €19) + kids' bikes/armor; the 9 & 12yo ride the free 6–12 course

Title: Sacra di San Michele
Description: 1,000-year-old abbey-fortress on a rock spike 1,000m over the Susa Valley; inspired The Name of the Rose. Climb the Staircase of the Dead.
How to get there: Day-trip — train to Sant'Ambrogio + shuttle up

Title: Truffle hunt with dogs — Langhe
Description: Hunt truffles with trained dogs — Sept/Oct is white-truffle season.
How to get there: Day-trip — train to Alba, operator pickup

Title: Forte di Bard
Description: An enormous fortress stacked up a mountain, with lifts up the rock face.
How to get there: Far — train + bus ~2h; better on its own trip

Title: Genoa — the Sacro Catino 'Holy Grail'
Description: A green-glass dish the Genoese swore for centuries was the actual Holy Grail, in the cathedral crypt.
How to get there: On the Turin→Chiavari day — central Genoa (open Tue, midday-closes)

Title: Genoa — walk through a real submarine
Description: Mediterranean's biggest maritime museum with a walk-through decommissioned Italian navy submarine moored afloat outside.
How to get there: On the Turin→Chiavari train day — you change in Genoa anyway; 10-min walk from Piazza Principe

Title: Cinque Terre sea-kayak — caves & cliffs
Description: Hop three villages on the card: Vernazza harbor and Doria castle, Manarola viewpoint and cove, Monterosso's sandy beach.
How to get there: Train to Monterosso/Riomaggiore + operator

Title: Make pesto by hand
Description: Learn to make real pesto by hand — mortar, pestle, Ligurian basil, pine nuts, Parmigiano and pecorino — then eat it over trofie.
How to get there: In the area — class in Levanto or Genoa

Title: Monterosso beach + the coastal ferry
Description: The one real Cinque Terre beach — swim, then hop a boat past the cliffs.
How to get there: Train ~50 min from Chiavari; ferry between villages

Title: Portofino Park family mountain-bike day
Description: Guided off-road MTB in the Parco di Portofino and the Tigullio hills — panoramic climbs and forest/coast descents; a guide picks kid-safe lines.
How to get there: Guided from your Chiavari base (operators meet in Chiavari/Sestri/Santa Margherita) — no car needed. Pre-confirm a 20"/24" kid MTB for Keir.

Title: Portovenere & the Byron Grotto
Description: Pastel houses, the cliff-edge church of San Pietro and Byron's Grotto below — gateway to the Muzzerone sea-cliffs.
How to get there: Train to La Spezia + boat/bus to Portovenere

Title: Rest and beach day on the Tigullio
Description: A no-travel day on Chiavari's broad beach and seafront promenade, drifting the arcaded medieval caruggi with gelato.
How to get there: On foot in Chiavari — zero trains

Title: Seafront trattoria di mare, Chiavari
Description: Waterfront trattoria in the base town — fritto misto, catch of the day, Ligurian pasta; book a table for six for Rhys's 18th.
How to get there: On foot in Chiavari, the coast base town — no transport needed.

Title: A stretch of the Blue Trail
Description: Walk just one leg — Monterosso-Vernazza is the classic scenic coastal hike; segments close after rain.
How to get there: Train to Monterosso, hike one leg, train the rest

Title: A swim / small-boat day
Description: Blue-flag coves — swim the Manarola cove, jump the rocks at Vernazza, or split a half-day private boat to hidden swim spots.
How to get there: Boats/coves reached from the Cinque Terre villages

Title: Antro del Corchia — Apuan Alps cave
Description: A huge karst cave system inside the marble mountains. Rockhound heaven.
How to get there: Day-trip — train toward Carrara + bus/taxi up; long

Title: Baia del Silenzio, Sestri Levante
Description: A Michelin-listed kitchen right on the Bay of Silence — the polished, grown-up way to mark 18; tightest on budget.
How to get there: Train 10 min east from Chiavari to Sestri Levante

Title: Camogli + the Portofino headland
Description: Tall trompe-l'oeil painted houses over a working fishing harbor, quieter than Portofino; pebble-beach swim and fried anchovies.
How to get there: Train ~25 min west from Chiavari to Camogli

Title: Camogli to San Fruttuoso by boat
Description: Little ferry around the Portofino headland to a road-less medieval abbey on the beach, with a swim and the Christ of the Abyss offshore.
How to get there: Train ~25 min west to Camogli, then ferry around the headland (calm-sea day)

Title: Christ of the Abyss snorkel, San Fruttuoso
Description: A bronze Christ stands on the seabed off the abbey cove; strong swimmers snorkel out, or peer down from a glass-bottom boat.
How to get there: Ferry to San Fruttuoso from Camogli/S. Margherita, then snorkel or glass-bottom boat

Title: Da Giovanni · abbey cove
Description: Tables on the boat-only beach beside a 10th-century abbey — a spectacular birthday LUNCH, since the last ferry out is ~5-6pm.
How to get there: Ferry from Camogli or Santa Margherita; confirm return boat time

Title: Ferry + gelato-and-focaccia crawl
Description: Let the boat do the walking — hop two or three villages by ferry with a focaccia slice and gelato in each.
How to get there: Village-to-village by ferry

Title: Finale Ligure — kids' MTB school (ages 7–11)
Description: World MTB hub; a children's mountain-bike school on the Manie plateau (coached by a multi-time world champ) plus shuttle-served flow trails for the big brothers.
How to get there: ~2h west by train (Finale Ligure Marina) + shuttle up to the plateau — a dedicated day. Schools supply age-right bikes.

Title: Focaccia di Recco and the pesto homeland
Description: Eat molten-cheese focaccia di Recco (IGP), farinata, and trofie al pesto in pesto's actual birthplace.
How to get there: Recco sits right on the Chiavari rail line

Title: Genova Aquarium
Description: Italy's biggest aquarium — sharks, dolphins, a rainforest biosphere.
How to get there: Day-trip — train to Genoa, Porto Antico

Title: Genova Righi Adventure Park
Description: A ropes course strung among Genoa's old hilltop fortifications.
How to get there: Day-trip — train to Genoa + Zecca–Righi funicular

Title: Grotte di Equi
Description: Caves right in the Apuan Alps.
How to get there: Day-trip — regional train to Equi Terme

Title: Guvano and hidden coves by kayak
Description: Paddle to road-less Guvano beach and inlets like Canneto and Fossola, or the hidden grotto by Vernazza — swim where crowds can't reach.
How to get there: Rent a kayak or water taxi from Vernazza or Monterosso, weather-dependent

Title: Il Gigante, the bombed sea-god
Description: A 46-foot 1910 concrete Neptune half-melted into the cliff — arms and trident torn off by WWII bombing; restored 2022.
How to get there: 5-min walk from Monterosso station on the Fegina seafront

Title: L'Altro Eden
Description: Boat-fresh Santa Margherita seafood in a harbor town with the easiest late train home — the low-stress 'safe special'.
How to get there: Train Chiavari to Santa Margherita 11-13 min, ~45/day

Title: Michelin room on the Bay of Silence
Description: Michelin-listed dining room overlooking the Baia del Silenzio at Sestri Levante.
How to get there: Train from Chiavari to Sestri Levante.

Title: Monterosso's salt-cured anchovies
Description: Slow Food Presidium anchovies packed in salt in chestnut barrels — fresh and buttery on warm focaccia; a Sept festival too.
How to get there: Monterosso trattorias and the September Sagra delle Acciughe Salate

Title: Ristorante dei Castelli
Description: Rhys's 18th on a medieval-castle terrace above both of Sestri's bays at sunset; order the catch of the day — no last-train stress.
How to get there: Train Chiavari to Sestri Levante 5-17 min, ~52/day

Title: Ristorante La Camogliese
Description: A wooden veranda built out over the rocks in Camogli, sunset over the Golfo Paradiso; local anchovies, day's catch, trofie al pesto.
How to get there: Train Chiavari to Camogli 15-20 min; reserve the veranda

Title: Santa Margherita / Portofino harbour dinner
Description: Dressy Riviera-postcard dinner over the harbour — the glam splurge option for the 18th.
How to get there: Short train to Santa Margherita Ligure, then bus/boat to Portofino.

Title: Sciacchetra and a terrace aperitivo
Description: The Cinque Terre's cult sweet wine from terrace-dried grapes; find a tasting or take a spritz to a cliff terrace at golden hour.
How to get there: Tastings in Manarola or Riomaggiore via the Cinque Terre Card

Title: The vineyard monorail trains
Description: One-person cog-rail monorails on stilts haul grapes down near-vertical terraces; mid-Sept harvest means they're running.
How to get there: Short train + walk to Volastra above Manarola; book a cellar visit

Title: The Way of the Sanctuaries
Description: Hilltop shrines above each village — Soviore over Monterosso is Liguria's oldest — linked by steep dry-stone trails with high, quiet views.
How to get there: Park trails climbing from each village, free; check trail status

Title: Torre Aurora, the pirate watchtower
Description: A ~year-1000 anti-Saracen watchtower on the headland, now a tiny cliff-edge lounge with 360 sea terraces for a sunset glass.
How to get there: Walk-up terrace in Monterosso; book a table for sunset

Title: Via dell'Amore, finally reopened
Description: The cliff-blasted lovers' walk between Riomaggiore and Manarola, shut 12 years, reopened 2024 — a short jaw-dropping sea ledge.
How to get there: On the Cinque Terre Card but needs a timed 30-min entry slot

Title: Village-hopping by ferry
Description: See the coast from the water: ferries link the Cinque Terre villages (bar Corniglia) and the Tigullio boats connect Chiavari, Portofino and Camogli.
How to get there: Golfo dei Poeti / Tigullio ferries from coastal stations

Title: Ristorante Belforte
Description: Tables built into a 1,000-year tower on Vernazza's cliff-tip hanging over the crashing sea — the most dramatic table on the coast.
How to get there: Train ~1h+ with one change; check the last train home. Closed Tue

Title: Sea-cliff climbing at Muzzerone
Description: A crag dropping straight into the Gulf of Poets — one of Italy's classic sea-cliff climbing spots, guided for total beginners up.
How to get there: Boat/bus to Portovenere; book a guided half-day

Title: Carrara — 4×4 marble quarry tour
Description: Ride a Land Rover into the working white-marble quarries. The operator can hold your bags.
How to get there: On the Chiavari→Florence train day — meet 7-min walk from Carrara-Avenza station

Title: Pietrasanta — the marble-carving town
Description: Sculptors' studios, bronze foundries, the free Museo dei Bozzetti.
How to get there: On the Chiavari→Florence day — historic centre across from the station

Title: Pisa — leaning tower + the death fresco
Description: Climb Pisa's famous leaning tower; easy day trip by rail from Florence.
How to get there: On the Chiavari→Florence day — you change at Pisa; bag storage at the station

Title: AquaFlor — build your own perfume
Description: Master perfumer walks you through 100+ essences to blend and bottle your own fragrance near Santa Croce; ~90 min.
How to get there: In Florence — walkable, near Santa Croce

Title: Bargello sculpture museum
Description: Donatello's David and great Renaissance sculpture in a former prison palace; calm and uncrowded. Under-18s free.
How to get there: In Florence — walkable in the centre

Title: Boboli and Bardini gardens
Description: Statues, grottoes and plants for Kei's botany; Bardini's wisteria terrace has the best rooftop view of the city.
How to get there: In Florence — ~10 min walk to Pitti/Boboli from base

Title: Brancacci Chapel + Oltrarno + Santo Spirito
Description: Masaccio's Renaissance-launching frescoes, a wander through the artisan quarter, then a Santo Spirito aperitivo.
How to get there: In Florence — Oltrarno, ~3 min walk from San Frediano base

Title: Brunelleschi's dome climb
Description: Climb Brunelleschi's 463-step dome and/or Giotto's campanile for the rival view; book the timed dome slot well ahead.
How to get there: In Florence — walkable; book a timed slot

Title: Buchette del vino — the wine windows
Description: Tiny 1500s arched wall hatches once used to sell wine tax-free; a few pour again — Babae on Via Santo Spirito is near base.
How to get there: In Florence — self-guided walk; Babae is near San Frediano base

Title: Florentine paper-marbling workshop
Description: Swirl and make your own marbled paper by hand.
How to get there: In Florence — central studios

Title: Fresh pasta + gelato class
Description: Hand-roll sfoglia and fold tortellini and tagliatelle at La Vecchia Scuola Bolognese or a Cesarine home class; book ahead.
How to get there: In Florence — central

Title: Hands-on artisan workshop
Description: Make something by hand: leather at Scuola del Cuoio, paper-marbling, bookbinding, mosaic or metal-embossing in the Oltrarno.
How to get there: In Florence — Oltrarno, walkable from San Frediano base

Title: HZERO — miniature railway world
Description: Enormous, obsessively detailed model railway and miniature city with trains and day-to-night lighting, in Palazzo Bombicci.
How to get there: In Florence — walkable in the centre

Title: Il Porcellino — rub the boar's nose
Description: Bronze boar in Mercato Nuovo; drop a coin through the grate for luck and rub his snout to guarantee a return to Florence.
How to get there: In Florence — 30-second detour by the leather market

Title: La Specola — minerals + anatomical waxes
Description: Taxidermy rooms and famed 18th-century wax anatomical models; newly reopened after restoration.
How to get there: In Florence — ~10-min walk from your door

Title: Le Arti Orafe — set your own gemstone
Description: Set a real gemstone onto a silver ring and take it home.
How to get there: In Florence — Oltrarno, walkable

Title: Mercato Centrale + San Lorenzo + gelato crawl
Description: Graze the upstairs food hall, browse San Lorenzo leather stalls, and run a gelato crawl (Vivoli, Perche No!, della Passera).
How to get there: In Florence — walkable, near San Lorenzo

Title: Museo Galileo
Description: Astrolabes, armillary spheres, early automata, Galileo's own telescopes, and his preserved finger in a glass egg.
How to get there: In Florence — by the Uffizi, walkable

Title: Officina di Santa Maria Novella — world's oldest pharmacy
Description: Dominican friars have brewed elixirs and perfumes here since 1221; frescoed sales rooms, old jars and a little museum.
How to get there: In Florence — walkable, by the train station

Title: ONE big-hitter: Uffizi OR Accademia
Description: Pick one: Botticelli's Birth of Venus and Primavera at the Uffizi, or Michelangelo's David at the Accademia. Under-18s free.
How to get there: In Florence — both walkable in the centre

Title: Palazzo Vecchio — secret passages
Description: Book the secret-passages / Monster tour through hidden staircases behind the state rooms, then climb the Arnolfo tower.
How to get there: In Florence — Piazza della Signoria, walkable

Title: Scuola del Cuoio — the leather school
Description: Jude's leatherworking: a working leather school inside Santa Croce runs hands-on craft sessions.
How to get there: In Florence — walk / short bus from San Frediano

Title: Stibbert Museum — armor and samurai
Description: Eccentric collector's villa crammed with European armor and a full hall of Japanese samurai armor and swords; uncrowded.
How to get there: In Florence — short bus ride out from the centre

Title: The Buontalenti Grotto in Boboli
Description: Mannerist fake cave with fake stalactites, sponge-stone figures and frescoed beasts, built for Francesco I de' Medici in the 1580s.
How to get there: In Florence — inside the Boboli Gardens, ~10 min from base

Title: The Vasari Corridor
Description: Medici's private elevated tunnel from Palazzo Vecchio over Ponte Vecchio to Pitti Palace; reopened Dec 2024. Max 5 tickets.
How to get there: In Florence — book Uffizi + corridor supplement well ahead

Title: The window that can never be closed
Description: On Piazza SS. Annunziata, a Palazzo Grifoni shutter has stood open ~500 years per a haunting bridal legend.
How to get there: In Florence — spot it from the piazza, walkable

Title: Uffizi family treasure hunt
Description: A kid-focused hunt that turns the Uffizi into a game.
How to get there: In Florence — the Uffizi

Title: Zecchi — the Renaissance color shop
Description: Artists'-supply shop on Via dello Studio still grinding pigments by hand, including ultramarine from ground lapis lazuli.
How to get there: In Florence — walkable, near the Duomo

Title: A Chianti / wine day
Description: Roll into the vineyards south of the city for a tasting and long lunch among the cypresses.
How to get there: Driver-led day out from Florence

Title: A Modena food morning
Description: Traditional balsamic acetaias in family attics, a Parmigiano dairy at dawn, and Massimo Bottura's home city.
How to get there: Day-trip — train from Florence, then ~30-min train Bologna to Modena

Title: Abetone Gravity Park — teens, September weekends only
Description: A real gondola gravity park in the Tuscan Apennines, but September is WEEKENDS-ONLY (Sep 19/20/26) and it's DH/enduro — good for the 16/18-yo, not a 9-yo. Phone to confirm the late-Sept bike weekends actually run.
How to get there: Florence→Pistoia→Abetone by bus, ~3h and sparse. Weekend of Sep 19-20 or 26 only.

Title: Archiginnasio + the Anatomical Theatre
Description: Old university hall walled with carved student coats-of-arms, hiding a wooden dissection theatre with a marble slab.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min train from Florence, then walk next to Piazza Maggiore

Title: Bike the walls of Lucca
Description: Ride the intact Renaissance city walls of Lucca; easy day trip by train from Florence.
How to get there: By train from Firenze S.M.N.

Title: Cassini's sundial and the unfinished facade (San Petronio)
Description: A 67 m brass meridian across San Petronio's floor, built by Cassini in 1655; a pinhole drops a sun-disc at solar noon.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min train from Florence, then walk to Piazza Maggiore

Title: Chianti hills — private family MTB
Description: Rolling forest-and-vineyard off-road on gentle gravel/trail; book a private family operator (kid pedal MTBs for Keir, e-MTBs for the teens) — most stock e-bike tours are 14+/165cm and exclude a 9-yo.
How to get there: Day-trip from Florence — operator collects you or starts near a train stop. Confirm a 24" kid MTB.

Title: Fiesole — Etruscan-Roman ruins
Description: Ride up to Fiesole for Etruscan-Roman ruins and hilltop views over Florence.
How to get there: Bus/rail up from Florence

Title: Gelato + Santo Stefano's seven churches
Description: A top-gelateria cone then the Basilica di Santo Stefano — a maze of seven interlinked churches and courtyards; free.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min train from Florence, then walk to Piazza Santo Stefano

Title: Gelato Museum Carpigiani
Description: World's first gelato museum: 20+ antique churning machines, the science of freezing, and hands-on batch-making workshops.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min train from Florence, then bus 87 (~20 min) to Anzola

Title: Grand Tour Italia food park
Description: The giant food park (the old FICO) on the edge of town — pizza and gelato made in front of you; re-check opening days.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min train from Florence, then local transit to the edge of town

Title: Il Ciocco Bike Park (Barga) — family trails + pump track
Description: Shuttle-served (no lift) but the best FAMILY bike experience on the route: Italy's largest indoor pump track, 70km incl. dedicated Easy & Family trails, qualified instructors, kids' rental.
How to get there: Day-trip/overnight from Florence — train to Lucca then Barga-Gallicano (~40-50 min) + a short resort shuttle up the hill. Confirm Sept shuttle days + kid bike stock.
Cost: Pump track €20/€15; trail rental + lesson extra

Title: La Finestrella di Via Piella
Description: A shuttered window opens onto a hidden canal between the houses — Bologna's 'Little Venice,' the last uncovered medieval waterway.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min train from Florence, then walk to Via Piella 16

Title: Labirinto della Masone — bamboo maze
Description: The largest bamboo labyrinth in the world.
How to get there: Day-trip — train to Parma + local; ~2h

Title: Modena — traditional balsamic acetaia
Description: Morning trip toward Modena to watch Parmigiano-Reggiano made at dawn and taste barrel-aged balsamic.
How to get there: Day-trip — train ~1h; book ahead

Title: Motor Valley — Ferrari · Lamborghini · Ducati
Description: Ferrari, Lamborghini and Ducati museums (Ducati in-city, Ferrari/Lamborghini toward Modena) — best as a dedicated car day.
How to get there: Day-trip — train to Bologna/Modena + Modenatur transfer

Title: Museo per la Memoria di Ustica
Description: A hushed hall rebuilt around a 1980 DC-9 wreck, wrapped in Boltanski's installation of 81 lights and mirrors for 81 victims; heavy.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min train from Florence, then 10-min walk from Bologna Centrale

Title: Osteria del Sole
Description: A 1465 wine-only bar hidden in the Quadrilatero: they pour, you bring food from surrounding market stalls to shared tables.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min train from Florence, then walk into the Quadrilatero

Title: Palazzo Poggi — the university's wunderkammer
Description: 18th-century anatomical wax models, obstetric figures, ship models, maps and natural-history oddities in a frescoed palace.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min train from Florence, then walk to via Zamboni

Title: Quadrilatero market food crawl
Description: Graze the medieval market lanes off Piazza Maggiore: cured meats at Tamburini, Mercato di Mezzo, a glass at Osteria del Sole.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min Frecciarossa from Florence, then walk to the market lanes off Piazza Maggiore

Title: Scarperia — knife & blade making
Description: A historic blade town with hands-on cutlery workshops.
How to get there: Day-trip — bus ~1h from Florence

Title: The feast — ragu, tortellini in brodo, mortadella
Description: A proper sit-down osteria: tagliatelle al ragu, tortellini in brodo, and real mortadella — the reason for the trip.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min train from Florence, then walk to a central osteria

Title: The porticoes — walk to San Luca
Description: UNESCO porticoes; the 3.8 km Portico di San Luca climbs 666 arches to a hilltop basilica, or ride the San Luca Express up.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min train from Florence, then walk or San Luca Express tourist train

Title: The three arrows of Corte Isolani
Description: Three ancient wooden arrows lodged in the ceiling beams of the dark medieval portico at Strada Maggiore 19, per a grisly legend.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min train from Florence, then walk to Strada Maggiore 19

Title: The tortellino and Venus's navel
Description: Legend says the tortellino was modelled on Venus's navel; order tortellini in brodo and settle the family fold debate.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min train from Florence, then any proper central osteria

Title: The Two Towers — climb Asinelli
Description: 498 wooden steps up the leaning Asinelli tower for the best view over the red rooftops; timed tickets, book ahead.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min train from Florence, then walk to Piazza di Porta Ravegnana

Title: The whispering telephone (Voltone del Podesta)
Description: Under the vaulted Voltone del Podesta, whisper into a diagonal corner and hear it perfectly across the square — a medieval acoustic trick.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min train from Florence, then walk to Piazza Maggiore

Title: Tuscan farm / cook day
Description: A farm or cooking day in the Tuscan countryside; easy from Florence.
How to get there: Day out in the countryside from Florence

Title: Volterra — carve alabaster
Description: Carve alabaster stone in the ancient Etruscan workshop town.
How to get there: Day-trip — train + bus ~2h; long

Title: Elba — Rio Marina mining park & minerals
Description: Red iron-rich Martian landscape, old mines, and mineral-collecting — Jude's dream island.
How to get there: Far — train to Piombino + ferry; an overnight, not a day-trip

Title: Orvieto — the double-helix well + caves
Description: The Pozzo di San Patrizio is two spiral staircases that never meet — plus Etruscan cave-tunnels.
How to get there: On the Florence→Rome train day — well is at the funicular top; station bag storage

Title: Aperitivo in Trastevere + Testaccio food
Description: Cesare al Casaletto, Flavio al Velavevodetto, Testaccio market — Rome's best eating, working-class and south of the center.
How to get there: In Rome — Metro B to Piramide (Testaccio) / tram 8 Trastevere

Title: Appia Antica off-road ride (Caffarella)
Description: Ride the ancient basalt Appian Way and the Caffarella valley dirt trails through a huge archaeological park — off-tarmac gravel and cobbles, ruins along the way.
How to get there: In Rome — bus to the park; EcoBike rents kids' bikes from age 4+ (120cm). Flat but genuinely off-road.

Title: Basilica di San Clemente — 3 layers down
Description: Descend through a church, an older church, and a pagan temple with a running stream.
How to get there: In Rome — near the Colosseum

Title: Bocca della Verita
Description: The giant ancient marble face at Santa Maria in Cosmedin that legend says bites off a liar's hand. Everyone takes the dare and the photo.
How to get there: In Rome — Metro B to Circo Massimo, walk

Title: Borghese Gallery
Description: Bernini's living marble (the Daphne) and Caravaggios in a garden villa. Timed entry, book well ahead. Adults and teens.
How to get there: In Rome — Metro A to Spagna, walk through Villa Borghese

Title: Capuchin Crypt — the bone chapel
Description: Five chapels on Via Veneto decorated entirely in friars' bones. Macabre and beautiful; gauge a sensitive 9-year-old.
How to get there: In Rome — Via Veneto, Metro A Barberini

Title: Castel Sant'Angelo
Description: Hadrian's tomb turned papal fortress: ramps, ramparts, a secret escape passage, dungeons, and the best rooftop view in Rome.
How to get there: In Rome — walkable from the Vatican

Title: Catacombs + Appian Way
Description: San Callisto or Domitilla: underground early-Christian tunnels, then bikes or a walk on the ancient road above.
How to get there: In Rome — bus 118 to San Callisto

Title: Centrale Montemartini
Description: Rome's first power station, now a museum where white marble gods stand among black diesel engines, turbines and boilers left in place.
How to get there: In Rome — Metro B Garbatella

Title: Colosseum Underground
Description: Down into the hypogeum — the tunnels and lifts beneath the arena floor.
How to get there: In Rome — Metro B Colosseo; book the special access

Title: Evening centro walk — Pantheon, Trevi, Navona
Description: The greatest free show in Rome after dark, gelato in hand; Giolitti near the Pantheon. Fits Rhys's first legal aperitivo.
How to get there: In Rome — Metro A to Spagna/Barberini, walk

Title: Explora Children's Museum + Villa Borghese
Description: Hands-on kids' museum, then rent a family rickshaw in the Borghese gardens. Good decompression for the 9-year-old.
How to get there: In Rome — Metro A to Flaminio, walk

Title: Galleria Doria Pamphilj
Description: A private palace still lived in, hung with Velazquez and Caravaggio, with a free audio guide by the prince himself. Calm, uncrowded.
How to get there: In Rome — Via del Corso, central, walk from Metro A

Title: Garbatella neighborhood
Description: 1920s garden-city courtyards and real Roman families away from the crush; Metro B to the Colosseum in 10 minutes.
How to get there: In Rome — Metro B to Garbatella

Title: Gladiator school — Scuola Gladiatori
Description: Gruppo Storico Romano: tunic, wooden sword, real moves, a mini-tournament and a certificate. Age 6+, so the 9-year-old clears it.
How to get there: In Rome — Via Appia Antica (bus 118)

Title: Museo delle Anime del Purgatorio
Description: One-room museum of scorched handprints and burn marks souls supposedly seared onto books and clothing to beg release from purgatory.
How to get there: In Rome — Lungotevere Prati, near Metro A Lepanto

Title: Museum of the Holy Souls in Purgatory
Description: A tiny, genuinely bizarre museum of scorch-marks 'left by souls'.
How to get there: In Rome — by Castel Sant'Angelo

Title: Palazzo Spada — the forced-perspective trick
Description: Borromini's optical-illusion colonnade that looks four times its real length.
How to get there: In Rome — Campo de' Fiori area

Title: Pizza + gelato class for kids
Description: Devour's family pasta class for the whole crew, or InRome's kids' pizza-and-gelato session. Good rainy-day or birthday move.
How to get there: In Rome — near Piazza Navona

Title: Pyramid of Cestius and Non-Catholic Cemetery
Description: A 2,000-year-old Egyptian-style pyramid tomb, and behind it an overgrown cemetery where Keats and Shelley sleep and cats nap on tombstones.
How to get there: In Rome — Metro B to Piramide

Title: Quartiere Coppede
Description: A hidden 1913-27 fantasy block: Art Nouveau meets Gothic meets Assyrian, a Fountain of the Frogs, a Fairy House and a spider-hung arch.
How to get there: In Rome — tram 3/19 to the Trieste district

Title: Quartiere Coppedè
Description: A fairy-tale quarter of monsters, spiders and dreamlike facades — free to wander.
How to get there: In Rome — tram/bus to Piazza Buenos Aires

Title: Roman Forum family treasure hunt
Description: The ancient core on one combo ticket; add the arena-floor or underground tour. 8:30am entry, book the timed combo ahead.
How to get there: In Rome — the Forum

Title: San Clemente's buried city
Description: Descend three stacked centuries under one church — 12th-c basilica over 4th-c church over 2nd-c house with a Mithras temple and a stream.
How to get there: In Rome — Metro B to Colosseo, short walk

Title: The Aventine Keyhole
Description: Peer through a locked green door at the Knights of Malta priory and a hedge tunnel frames St Peter's dome — three states in one glance.
How to get there: In Rome — Metro B to Circo Massimo, walk up the Aventine

Title: The Catacombs
Description: Kilometres of early-Christian burial tunnels under the city.
How to get there: In Rome — Via Appia (bus 118) or S. Agnese

Title: Torre Argentina cat sanctuary
Description: In the sunken square where Julius Caesar was stabbed, ~150 rescued cats lounge among temple ruins; new walkways and a volunteer shelter.
How to get there: In Rome — tram 8 / bus to Largo Argentina

Title: Vatican Museums + Sistine Chapel + St Peter's
Description: Vast collection done as a kid-paced highlights route; 8am early entry, no Wednesdays. Don't miss the frescoed Gallery of Maps.
How to get there: In Rome — Metro A to Ottaviano

Title: Bomarzo — the Park of the Monsters
Description: Renaissance monster park of giant grotesque stone sculptures; the parents' bucket list and genuinely fun for kids.
How to get there: Day-trip — train to Orte/Viterbo + bus; ~1h30

Title: Calcata
Description: A hippie cliff-village of artists in a medieval hill town — bohemian, weird and charming, on the parents' bucket list.
How to get there: Bus from Rome (Saxa Rubra) toward Calcata

Title: Civita di Bagnoregio — the 'dying city'
Description: The 'dying city' perched on an eroding tuff pinnacle, reached by a footbridge. A dramatic day-trip wander.
How to get there: Day-trip — train to Orvieto + bus

Title: Falconer for a Day — La Selvotta
Description: A bird of prey flies free and lands back on your glove. Under 20km from Rome.
How to get there: Day-trip — needs a taxi/transfer (~20km NW)

Title: Tarot Garden (Giardino dei Tarocchi)
Description: Niki de Saint Phalle's giant mosaic tarot sculptures in a Tuscan garden. Surreal, walkable and photogenic.
How to get there: Train to Capalbio Scalo, then short taxi/walk

Title: Frasassi Caves — the Ancona Abyss
Description: A limestone chamber big enough to hold Milan Cathedral. Marquee cave for the rockhound.
How to get there: Far — train to Genga ~3h+; better on its own trip

Title: Pitigliano + the Vie Cave
Description: A town carved from volcanic tufa, ringed by Etruscan roads cut as deep trenches through the rock.
How to get there: Far — train + bus ~2h30; better as its own outing

Title: Ferrara — Castello Estense
Description: A moated brick castle you go inside: drawbridges, the dungeon cells where the d'Este princes were locked up, painted ceilings, and the Torre dei Leoni tower climb.
How to get there: On the Rome→Venice train day — Ferrara is on the line; 15-min walk or 5-min bus from the station, bag storage at the station.

Title: Ferrara — Palazzo dei Diamanti
Description: A palace faced with 8,500 pyramid-cut marble 'diamonds' laid so the light shifts as you walk past — pure Escher/sacred-geometry; the Pinacoteca Nazionale is inside.
How to get there: On the Rome→Venice day — ~10-min walk from Castello Estense, central Ferrara.

Title: Ferrara — Via delle Volte & the city walls
Description: A long, dark medieval covered street of brick archways, plus 9km of intact Renaissance walls you can walk or bike — UNESCO 'ideal city', flat and bike-mad.
How to get there: On the Rome→Venice day — in Ferrara's compact centre, walkable; rent bikes to ride the walls.

Title: Borges Labyrinth — San Giorgio Maggiore
Description: A hedge maze based on the Borges story, on its own island.
How to get there: In Venice — vaporetto to San Giorgio; book ahead

Title: Cannaregio and the Jewish Ghetto
Description: The world's first ghetto, quiet canals and the best cicchetti bars on Fondamenta della Misericordia; lived-in Venice at aperitivo hour.
How to get there: Vaporetto to Cannaregio

Title: Carnival mask-making workshop
Description: The Dorsoduro atelier that made masks for Kubrick's Eyes Wide Shut runs hands-on courses to build and decorate your own Carnival mask.
How to get there: In Venice — central studios

Title: Climb the Campanile + clock tower
Description: The bell-tower lift for the big view, plus the Torre dell'Orologio tour inside the blue-and-gold astronomical clock mechanism.
How to get there: Vaporetto to San Marco

Title: Doge's Palace — Secret Itineraries
Description: Gilded halls, Bridge of Sighs, dungeons and 2,000+ arms and armor; the Secret Itineraries tour adds the prisons.
How to get there: In Venice — vaporetto to San Marco; book the tour

Title: Get lost on purpose
Description: No itinerary: hand the kids a map and let them navigate the back-canal labyrinth to a gelato. Venice is the safest big city to wander.
How to get there: On foot from any vaporetto stop

Title: Grand Canal by vaporetto (Line 1)
Description: The cheapest grand tour in the world — ride the slow boat end to end past the palazzi; a gondola once for the romance.
How to get there: Vaporetto Line 1

Title: Hidden-city treasure hunt
Description: Secret symbols, alleys and clues across Venice.
How to get there: In Venice — self-guided from a start point

Title: Homo Faber (if dates align)
Description: Venice's master-craft biennial on San Giorgio — the best craft show in Europe; check whether it overlaps the Oct 3-10 window.
How to get there: Vaporetto to San Giorgio Maggiore

Title: Kayak the lagoon & hidden canals
Description: Paddle the quiet back-canals and out into the lagoon.
How to get there: In Venice — operator meeting point

Title: Learn to row Venetian-style
Description: A standing-up rowing lesson in a traditional boat.
How to get there: In Venice — operator meeting point

Title: Libreria Acqua Alta
Description: Early October tides can flood St Mark's; the city's answer is instant elevated walkways (passerelle) on trestles. Check the tide app, pack boots.
How to get there: Vaporetto + walk to Castello

Title: Lido beach + vaporetto rides
Description: An actual beach island with rentable bikes and room to run — the low-key counterweight to museum days, and where the family is.
How to get there: In Venice — you're based on the Lido

Title: Murano — watch glassblowing, make a bead
Description: Watch a maestro shape molten glass, then try it: a furnace class for teens (Wave) or a torch-bead bench for younger kids (VivoVenetia, 10+).
How to get there: In Venice — vaporetto to Murano; bead class age 10+ (email re Keir)

Title: Natural History Museum
Description: Dinosaurs and a giant whale skeleton in a Grand Canal palazzo — an easy rainy-day hit for the 9-year-old.
How to get there: Vaporetto to San Stae

Title: Peggy Guggenheim / Accademia
Description: Modern art in Peggy's compact canal-side home, or the Venetian masters at the Accademia; the grown-ups' art fix.
How to get there: Vaporetto to Dorsoduro/Accademia

Title: Rialto market + cicchetti crawl
Description: The morning fish-and-produce market, then a hands-on cicchetti cooking class in a local's home (Cesarine) or a tasting walk.
How to get there: Vaporetto to Rialto (San Polo/Dorsoduro)

Title: Scala Contarini del Bovolo
Description: A hidden 15th-c external spiral staircase — 80 stone steps up a 26m tower to a rooftop belvedere. Timed 30-min slots, max 20.
How to get there: In Venice — near San Marco, walkable

Title: Scuola Grande di San Rocco
Description: Tintoretto's overwhelming cycle of canvases — 'Venice's Sistine Chapel,' and rarely crowded.
How to get there: Vaporetto + walk (San Polo)

Title: Squero di San Trovaso
Description: One of Venice's last working gondola boatyards, open since the 17th c; watch craftsmen build gondolas from the bank across Rio San Trovaso.
How to get there: Vaporetto to Zattere (Dorsoduro)

Title: St Mark's Basilica + golden mosaics
Description: 8,000 sq m of gold Byzantine mosaic ceiling in Piazza San Marco; book a timed slot and add the Pala d'Oro and terrace.
How to get there: Vaporetto to San Marco

Title: The traghetto crossing
Description: The locals' hack: a two-oared traghetto gondola ferries you across the Grand Canal for ~€2, standing the whole way. A real gondola ride for pocket change.
How to get there: Traghetto at one of 7 crossing points

Title: The Venetian Arsenal
Description: The enormous medieval shipyard that once built a galley a day.
How to get there: In Venice — Castello district, walkable

Title: Venetian cicchetti cooking class
Description: Make the city's own bar snacks in a local's home.
How to get there: In Venice — Dorsoduro (Cesarine host home)

Title: Burano + Torcello islands
Description: Burano's candy-colored fishing houses and lace-making, plus quiet Torcello with its ancient mosaic cathedral; a relaxed all-day boat outing.
How to get there: Vaporetto north to Burano/Torcello

Title: Burano's crooked campanile and Lace Museum
Description: Burano's visibly leaning bell tower plus the Lace Museum on Galuppi Square where Buranese women still demonstrate needle-lace by hand.
How to get there: Vaporetto 12 to Burano

Title: Canalside anniversary dinner, Venice
Description: Romantic waterside table on a quiet rio in Cannaregio or Dorsoduro — seafood and wine, water lapping past the railing.
How to get there: Vaporetto from the Lido into Venice.

Title: Colli Euganei — MTB in the volcanic hills
Description: The real trail terrain near Venice: forest singletrack and gravel climbs over the Euganean Hills, with a marked MTB circuit — gentler perimeter gravel for Keir, hills for the teens.
How to get there: Day-trip — ~40-min train Venice→Este/Monselice/Montegrotto, then local bike hire.

Title: Grotte di Oliero — by boat
Description: Cave springs you enter by boat. Rockhound + water.
How to get there: Day-trip — train + bus ~1h30

Title: Museo del Precinema — magic lanterns
Description: Magic lanterns and proto-cinema devices in Padua.
How to get there: Day-trip — 30-min train to Padua

Title: Museo Nicolis — cars & machines
Description: Cars, motorcycles and machines near Verona.
How to get there: Day-trip — train to Verona + local

Title: Padua day-trip
Description: 25 min by train: Giotto's Scrovegni Chapel frescoes, the vast Prato della Valle, and the world's oldest botanical garden.
How to get there: Train to Padova

Title: San Michele — the cemetery island
Description: Venice's walled island of the dead: cypress avenues, a white Renaissance church, and graves of Stravinsky, Diaghilev and Ezra Pound.
How to get there: Vaporetto 4.1/4.2 from Fondamente Nove

Title: San Pelagio — Minotaur & mirror mazes
Description: Two very different mazes at a castle near Padua.
How to get there: Day-trip — train to Padua + local

Title: The plague islands by boat
Description: Private 'ghost island' boat tours circle sealed Poveglia's ruins and land at Lazzaretto Vecchio, Venice's plague quarantine islands.
How to get there: Private boat tour from Venice

Title: Torcello's Devil's Bridge and Attila's throne
Description: Venice's birthplace island hides a railless 'Devil's Bridge' and a marble 'throne of Attila' — sit in it and legend says you'll return.
How to get there: Vaporetto 12 + 9 via Burano

Title: Villa Pisani labyrinth — Stra
Description: A famous historic hedge maze with a tower at the centre.
How to get there: Day-trip — train/bus toward Padua, ~45 min

Title: Grotta Gigante — the giant cavern
Description: A karst cavern big enough to hold a cathedral.
How to get there: Far — train to Trieste ~2h + bus; better as its own trip

Title: A family hike + a rifugio lunch
Description: An easy, lift-assisted meadow trail ending at a mountain hut for terrace lunch — Kaiserschmarrn, apple strudel, canederli dumplings.
How to get there: Gentle trails off any lift

Title: Tschötscherhof — Grey's 12th birthday dinner
Description: ★ THE PICK for Oct 12. A 500-year-old family-run farm inn in the hamlet of St. Oswald: Tyrolean farm cooking from their own land — speck, canederli dumplings, roasts, mountain cheese — in a low-beamed stube. Rated 9.1. This is the meaty, cheesy, cosy opposite of a tasting menu, and it is a listed Törggelen house, so mid-October is exactly its season.
How to get there: Drive ~10 min to St. Oswald, Kastelruth. CONFIRMED open 21 Jun – 2 Nov 2026 daily; warm kitchen 12:00–14:00 and 18:00–20:30 only, so book an early table.

Title: Alpe di Siusi — Europe's biggest meadow
Description: Take bikes up the big cable cars onto the plateau for gentle high-meadow gravel and Seceda descents — the bike day that still works after the flow-trail lifts shut.
How to get there: The Siusi cableway, 8 min from the Singerhof (car road up closed 9–5, reopens 17:00)

Title: Cable cars, plural
Description: Half the magic is the ride up — Seceda, Mont Seuc, Alpe di Siusi, Renon: big glass cabins swinging over pastures with almost no walking.
How to get there: Various gondolas from Ortisei and Bolzano

Title: Col Raiser + Puez-Odle walks
Description: A quieter gondola into the nature park, under the Odle spires.
How to get there: Gondola from Santa Cristina — ~10 min drive

Title: Gostner Schwaige — alpine dairy hut
Description: A working hut making its own cheese, butter and ricotta — a special mountain lunch.
How to get there: Siusi cableway (8 min away) to Compatsch + hut bus/walk; drive up after 17:00

Title: Hike & Cheese Workshop
Description: Make fresh cheese by hand with a farmer (in English). Grey's Oct 12 birthday centrepiece.
How to get there: Guided — private transfer + cable car included

Title: Museum Gherdëina — Ortisei
Description: Local Dolomite fossils and minerals — a good rainy-day fix.
How to get there: In Ortisei — walkable

Title: Sassolungo — the 'coffin lift'
Description: Tiny open two-person cabins float you to a high saddle. Closes Oct 11 — ride it your first day.
How to get there: Drive ~25–30 min to Passo Sella

Title: Seceda — the knife-edge ridge
Description: Two-stage lift from Ortisei to the surreal tilted-blade ridgeline at 2,500 m — one of Earth's most photographed skylines, little climbing up top.
How to get there: Drive ~25 min to Ortisei, then the two-stage gondola

Title: Toboggan runs + playgrounds
Description: Val Gardena's Alpine adventure parks and mountain playgrounds, plus a summer-toboggan run if still open — Keir and Grey fuel.
How to get there: Around Val Gardena

Title: Trail Arena Val Gardena — family flow trails
Description: Your home valley's flow-trail bike park (graded 'Family Line' + freeride). CATCH: the bike gondola (Dantercepies) closes Oct 4 — shut before you arrive Oct 10, so no lift-served laps on your dates. Use Kronplatz for lifts; self-pedal/e-bike flow only here.
How to get there: Drive ~30 min from Kastelruth — but the Dantercepies bike gondola shuts Oct 4, so no lift-served laps; see Kronplatz.

Title: Val Gardena villages + Ladin woodcarving
Description: Three storybook villages speaking Ladin; wander pedestrian centers and watch a woodcarver at work in the valley's centuries-old craft.
How to get there: Base valley — Ortisei, Santa Cristina, Selva

Title: Watch a woodcarver work
Description: Ortisei has carved wood for 400 years; duck into a workshop or the local museum to watch a saint or nativity emerge from a block.
How to get there: Museum Gherdeina / workshops, Ortisei

Title: Wine on a sunny hut terrace
Description: An hour on a rifugio terrace with Lagrein or Gewurztraminer, a speck-and-cheese board, and a wall of dolomite in front of you.
How to get there: Any rifugio terrace off a lift

Title: Bletterbach — the fossil canyon
Description: The 'Grand Canyon of South Tyrol': a 400-m gorge slicing through 280-million-year-old rock, with fossils and textbook-clear geology. UNESCO geosite.
How to get there: Drive ~1h–1h15 (great use of the car)

Title: Castel Roncolo / Schloss Runkelstein
Description: The 'illustrated castle': largest secular medieval fresco cycle in the Alps — knights, courtly life, Tristan and Isolde — on a crag-top fortress. Under-14 free.
How to get there: Drive — just outside Bolzano

Title: Cinque Torri open-air war museum
Description: A whole WWI front line — restored trenches, gun emplacements and tunnels you climb through — among five toppling rock towers. Free, outdoors.
How to get there: Drive ~1h15 toward Cortina + short chairlift from Bai de Dones

Title: Dolomiti Paganella Bike Park (Andalo)
Description: A big family MTB complex — 25 trails, huge skills areas, pump tracks, beginner/family zones — and one of the very few alpine parks open to Nov 2. The backup to Kronplatz on the car leg.
How to get there: Drive ~2h down the A22 from Kastelruth (the car leg). The backup park only — Kronplatz is half the drive.

Title: Earth Pyramids of Ritten
Description: Clay hoodoos — tall earthen spires each capped by a balancing boulder, pure Escher geology. Made for Jude the rockhound.
How to get there: Renon cable car from Bolzano + narrow-gauge Renon railway

Title: Get buried in a hay bath
Description: In Fie/Vols they've wrapped people in warm, damp, fermenting mountain hay since 1903 — lie packed in it and sweat while alpine herbs work. Gross-cool.
How to get there: Drive ~25 min to Vols (Heubad hotel spa)

Title: Kronplatz Bike Park — lift-served MTB
Description: 18 lift-served mountain-bike trails off the Olang gondola, with skills parks to practise on before going up, plus rentals and a bike school. Crucially it runs to 8 Nov — nearly every other Alpine bike park has shut by then, so this is the ONE real park open on your dates.
How to get there: ★ CRITICAL — LOCKED for Sun Oct 11, weather backup Tue Oct 13. Drive ~1h20 from the Singerhof in Kastelruth via Waidbruck, the A22 and the Puster valley. Reserve 20-inch and 24-inch kid bikes plus armour ahead.
Cost: gondola + kid bike hire (call re: which of the 18 trails suit a 9-yo)

Title: Lagazuoi — WWI tunnels in the mountain
Description: Ride to 2,778 m and walk the WWI front tunnels blasted through the summit — sweeping panorama, sobering history. Confirm the lift runs mid-October.
How to get there: Drive ~1h to Passo Falzarego + cable car

Title: Lago di Braies
Description: Mirror-still emerald lake with wooden rowboats and a flat lakeside loop — peak reflection-symmetry beauty; confirm road/boats haven't closed for the season.
How to get there: Drive to Braies (Prags)

Title: Lago di Carezza
Description: Tiny turquoise-glowing lake beneath the Latemar, an easy roadside stop closer to base.
How to get there: Drive — roadside stop beneath the Latemar

Title: Messner Mountain Museum Firmian
Description: Reinhold Messner's spiralling museum in ruined Sigmundskron castle — a labyrinth of towers, staircases and terraces with Tibetan art and summit relics.
How to get there: Drive ~40 min to Bolzano

Title: Museum Ladin Ciastel de Tor
Description: A castle museum on the Ladins and their mythology — the lost Kingdom of Fanes, marmot-princesses — alongside the geology that built the Dolomites.
How to get there: Drive ~55 min to Val Badia

Title: Otzi the Iceman
Description: A real 5,300-year-old glacier mummy with his actual clothes, tools and copper axe, viewed through a frozen window. Ideal bad-weather backup.
How to get there: Drive to South Tyrol Museum of Archaeology, Bolzano

Title: Ridnaun mine world + the show tunnel
Description: One of Europe's highest mines (silver, lead, zinc to 1985); helmet up, walk 200 m into a real ore tunnel, watch Victorian ore-crushers clank to life.
How to get there: Drive ~1h to Ratschings

Title: Roter Hahn farm — bread & strudel baking
Description: A hands-on farm baking session, arranged directly — apple-harvest season.
How to get there: Drive ~5–15 min around Kastelruth; email a farm ahead

Title: The great scenic drives
Description: Hairpin up the Gardena and Sella passes, loop the legendary Sellaronda around the Sella massif, and top out at Passo Pordoi. Jude's dream drive.
How to get there: Drive — Gardena and Sella passes, Sellaronda, Passo Pordoi

Title: Törggelen — the autumn farm dinner
Description: October-only: roast chestnuts, new wine and strudel at a farm tavern.
How to get there: Drive ~30–50 min to the Eisacktal

Title: Torggelen at a mountain farm
Description: South Tyrol's autumn ritual: walk to a farmhouse inn for young cloudy wine, roasted chestnuts, speck, dumplings and doughnuts by a wood stove.
How to get there: Drive to farms around Bolzano/Isarco (Red Rooster network)

Title: Trauttmansdorff Gardens + Touriseum
Description: Empress Sissi's terraced castle gardens in themed worlds — rainforest greenhouse, lily pond, cactus deserts — plus a tourism museum with playful dioramas.
How to get there: Drive ~1h to Merano

Title: Val di Fassa / Predazzo — geology trails
Description: Volcanic and sedimentary Dolomite geology with a mineral museum.
How to get there: Drive ~45 min

Title: Via ferrata — Averau / Gran Cir
Description: An approachable first via ferrata for the teens, with a guide (weather permitting).
How to get there: Drive + guided; weather-dependent mid-Oct

Title: The drowned village of Reschensee
Description: A single medieval bell tower stands alone in a lake — all that shows of Graun, flooded in 1950 for a dam; legend says the bells still ring on winter nights.
How to get there: Drive ~2h each way to the Vinschgau

Title: Crespi d'Adda — the company town frozen in 1878
Description: A whole UNESCO World Heritage village built by one cotton family for its workers: identical brick houses each with its own garden plot, a school, a washhouse, a company cemetery, and the owners' fake castle glowering down the main street at all of it.
How to get there: Metro M1 to Lampugnano, then the Z301 Milan–Bergamo coach to the A4 Capriate stop (~45 min) and a 20-min walk down into the village.
Cost: Village free to walk · guided tour ~€10pp

Title: Bergamo — walk the Venetian walls
Description: Six kilometres of 16th-century Venetian ramparts wrap the hilltop Città Alta and you can walk the whole circuit — UNESCO World Heritage, with gun-galleries hollowed out under the bastions and a funicular to save the climb.
How to get there: Train Milano Centrale→Bergamo ~50 min, then the funicular from Viale Vittorio Emanuele up into the old town.

Title: Sacro Monte di Varese — the chapel staircase
Description: A cobbled two-kilometre pilgrim ramp climbing past fourteen domed chapels, each one packed with life-size painted terracotta figures frozen mid-scene like a 400-year-old diorama. One of the nine Sacri Monti on the UNESCO World Heritage list.
How to get there: Train Milano Cadorna→Varese ~1h, city bus C to Prima Cappella, then walk up — or the Vellone funicular, which only runs weekends (Sat Sep 12 works).

Title: Brescia — Santa Giulia and the Winged Victory
Description: A Lombard convent built on top of a Roman house, now a museum you walk down through in layers — mosaic floors, the jewelled Cross of Desiderius — and in the Roman temple next door a life-size bronze Winged Victory. Part of the UNESCO World Heritage 'Longobards in Italy'.
How to get there: Train Milano Centrale→Brescia ~40 min on a fast train, then metro or a 15-min walk to Via dei Musei.

Title: Monte San Giorgio fossils — Besano
Description: A UNESCO World Heritage mountain made of Middle Triassic seabed. The village museum has the six-metre Besanosaurus with four unborn babies still inside her ribcage, plus fish and marine reptiles split out of the black shale on the slope above.
How to get there: Train Milano Porta Garibaldi→Porto Ceresio ~1h20, then a short bus or taxi the last 3 km to Besano — a long half-day, but the only fossil World Heritage site in reach.

Title: Palazzo Reale + the Royal Armoury
Description: The Savoys' own palace on Piazza Castello — gilded state rooms, Guarini's black spiral Chapel of the Shroud, and a 100-metre gallery of jousting armour and armoured horses that is one of the best in Europe. A UNESCO World Heritage Savoy residence, minutes from the flat.
How to get there: In Turin — Piazza Castello, a few minutes' walk from the base.

Title: Reggia di Venaria — the Savoy hunting palace
Description: Piedmont's answer to Versailles and UNESCO World Heritage: an 80-metre barrel-vaulted Great Gallery of white stucco and glass, stables built like a cathedral, and gardens big enough to let four boys off the leash. CLOSED MONDAYS — which is your one clear Turin day, so check the dates before banking on it.
How to get there: Venaria Express shuttle from Piazza Castello ~40 min (Tue–Sun), or GTT bus 11/72 on an ordinary urban ticket.

Title: Ivrea — the Olivetti company town
Description: Adriano Olivetti built an entire modernist city around his typewriter factory — glass-walled workshops, workers' housing, canteen, nursery — and it is now UNESCO World Heritage. The open-air route along Via Jervis is free; the museum has the typewriters and Italy's first computers.
How to get there: Train Torino Porta Susa→Ivrea ~1h; Via Jervis starts a 15-min walk from the station. Pairs with the Damanhur day.
Cost: Open-air route free · museum small charge

Title: Genoa — the Palazzi dei Rolli on Via Garibaldi
Description: A street of merchant-prince palaces so grand the Republic kept official lists — the rolli — and drew lots to decide which one had to house a visiting king. UNESCO World Heritage; three of them on Via Garibaldi are now one museum, with a rooftop terrace over the port.
How to get there: On the Turin→Chiavari train day — you change in Genoa anyway; Via Garibaldi is a 10-min walk from Piazza Principe.

Title: Villa La Petraia + Villa di Castello
Description: Two Medici villas on the hillside above the city, both UNESCO World Heritage: Petraia's courtyard is roofed in glass over a fresco cycle of Medici history, and Castello's garden hides a grotto walled with mosaic animals — a whole stone ark of them. Free to get in.
How to get there: In Florence — bus 28 from Santa Maria Novella, ~25 min up Via Reginaldo Giuliani; check the Monday closures.

Title: Siena — Piazza del Campo and the striped Duomo
Description: A UNESCO World Heritage medieval city built around a brick shell of a square you can lie down in. The cathedral is banded black and white like a humbug, its floor is 56 inlaid marble pictures, and the Facciatone stairs put you on top of a cathedral that was never finished.
How to get there: Autolinee Toscane rapid coach from Florence ~1h15 direct, or train ~1h30 with a change at Empoli.

Title: San Gimignano — the town of towers
Description: Fourteen medieval stone tower-houses still stand out of the seventy-odd rival families built to out-do each other — UNESCO World Heritage. Climb the Torre Grossa, then eat the gelato that has won the world championship more than once.
How to get there: Train Florence→Poggibonsi ~1h, then bus 130 up the hill ~25 min.

Title: Modena — the Duomo and the Ghirlandina
Description: UNESCO World Heritage Romanesque: Wiligelmo carved the whole book of Genesis across the facade in the 1100s, stone lions hold the porch up, and the leaning Ghirlandina tower next door is ~200 steps of climb. Bolt it onto the balsamic-and-Parmigiano morning.
How to get there: Day-trip — 37-min train from Florence to Bologna, then ~25 min on to Modena; the Duomo is a 15-min walk from the station.

Title: Val d'Orcia + Pienza
Description: The cypress-line-and-clay-hill Tuscany off every postcard is itself UNESCO World Heritage, and so is Pienza — a whole Renaissance town centre a pope rebuilt out of his own birthplace in four years. Also where the pecorino comes from.
How to get there: Far — carless it's a train to Chiusi (~1h45) plus a sparse country bus; realistically a hired driver and a whole day.

Title: San Paolo fuori le Mura
Description: The outlying piece named in Rome's UNESCO World Heritage listing: a vast basilica over St Paul's tomb, ringed above the columns by mosaic portrait medallions of every pope in order — and the empty slots left at the end feed the legend that the world ends when they run out.
How to get there: In Rome — Metro B to Basilica San Paolo, the church is at the top of the steps.

Title: Villa d'Este — the fountain garden at Tivoli
Description: A hillside terraced into hundreds of fountains that run on gravity alone — a wall of a hundred spouts, and a water organ that still plays itself on the hour. UNESCO World Heritage, and the best soaking-wet afternoon within an hour of Rome.
How to get there: Train Roma Tiburtina→Tivoli ~1h, then 10 min uphill on foot; or Cotral coach from Metro B Ponte Mammolo.

Title: Hadrian's Villa (Villa Adriana)
Description: An emperor's 120-hectare private country town, UNESCO World Heritage: a long colonnaded pool watched over by marble crocodiles, bath halls with the domes still on, and an island villa Hadrian could pull the bridges up on when he wanted to be left alone. Huge — wear real shoes.
How to get there: Same Tivoli day as Villa d'Este — CAT bus 4/4X down from the town centre, ~15 min.

Title: Cerveteri — the Banditaccia tomb streets
Description: A UNESCO World Heritage Etruscan city of the dead laid out like a real town, with lanes between grass-topped burial mounds. Duck through the doorways and the rooms inside are carved with stone beds, pillows and cooking pots so the dead would feel at home.
How to get there: Train Roma San Pietro→Ladispoli-Cerveteri ~50 min, then a local bus into Cerveteri and up to the necropolis — or a direct Cotral coach, ~1h.

Title: Tarquinia — the painted Etruscan tombs
Description: Same UNESCO World Heritage listing as Cerveteri, opposite experience: you go down steep steps into sealed chambers and press up against the glass at 2,500-year-old wall paintings of dancers, leopards, a boy diving off a rock, and banquets — still in colour.
How to get there: Direct regional train Roma Termini→Tarquinia ~1h20, then a bus up to the hill town and a walk out to the Monterozzi necropolis.
Cost: Under-18 EU free · adults ~€6 with the museum

Title: Vicenza — Palladio's city + La Rotonda
Description: The UNESCO World Heritage city one architect rebuilt. The Teatro Olimpico's permanent wooden stage set is a fake street built in forced perspective that shrinks to child-size at the back, and La Rotonda on the edge of town is the four-porch villa half the world's parliaments were copied from.
How to get there: Train Venezia→Vicenza — ~25 min on a Frecciarossa out of Mestre, ~1h05 regional; everything but La Rotonda is walkable from the station.

Title: Villa Foscari 'La Malcontenta'
Description: A Palladian villa standing with its feet almost in the Brenta, on the same UNESCO World Heritage listing as Vicenza — named for a Foscari wife supposedly shut up out here in disgrace, and frescoed floor to ceiling with giants inside.
How to get there: ACTV/ATVO bus from Piazzale Roma toward Mira, ~40 min, then a 10-min walk. Open Apr–Oct, closed Mondays, mornings plus mid-afternoon — email to book at least ten days ahead.

Title: Verona — the Arena and the Roman city
Description: A UNESCO World Heritage city still sitting on its Roman bones: the 1st-century Arena holds 15,000 and you climb the original stone tiers, and Castelvecchio's red-brick bridge marches across the Adige on swallowtail battlements.
How to get there: Train Venezia→Verona Porta Nuova — ~1h10 fast, ~1h30 regional; the Arena is a 15-min walk from the station.

Title: Prosecco Hills of Conegliano and Valdobbiadene
Description: UNESCO World Heritage farmland: near-vertical grass 'hogback' ridges cut into vine strips too steep for any tractor, so the harvest still comes down on foot and by cable. Mid-October catches the tail of the picking.
How to get there: On the Oct 10 drive Venice→Kastelruth — the A27 runs straight past Conegliano; take the Strada del Prosecco west toward Valdobbiadene for an hour and rejoin the motorway.
Cost: Free to drive · cellar tastings vary

Title: Sciliar–Catinaccio — the World Heritage massif above the house
Description: The flat-topped Schlern and the Rosengarten spires you can see from the Singerhof are one of the nine mountain systems in the Dolomites UNESCO World Heritage listing — fossil reefs that were a tropical sea floor. Watch them turn blood-red at sunset; the Ladins call it the enrosadira.
How to get there: From the door in Kastelruth — or drive 10 min down to Seis and take the Alpe di Siusi cable car for the foot of the Schlern.

Title: Bistrot B24 fromagerie — fondue & raclette
Description: The fondue answer, and it also does pizza — so it hits both of Grey's loves at one table. Chef Norbert Dejaco keeps an in-house fromagerie: a small private room with a heating element in every table and its own ventilation, serving cheese fondue or classic raclette. WARNING: evenings only, and the autumn season dates are unconfirmed — Val Gardena half-shuts between seasons, so phone +39 0471 774444 before building the birthday around it.
How to get there: Drive ~35 min to Selva, Puez Str. 24. Evening only. VERIFY it is open on Oct 12 — call +39 0471 774444 or info@bistrot24.eu.

Title: Pizzeria Bachler — the 5-minute pizza fallback
Description: If the fondue is shut or the day runs long: the best-regarded pizzeria in Kastelruth, wood-fired, with a terrace looking at the mountains. Five minutes from the house. Zur Alten Schmiede in the village centre is the other good one — Italian and Tyrolean side by side, generous plates, wood oven.
How to get there: Drive ~5 min into Kastelruth. No booking drama, and it works on any night.

Title: Abinea day spa — Dan & Kei's massage
Description: The one thing on this leg that is just for the two of us, and it is five minutes from the house in Castelrotto. Day Spa for non-residents is EUR 65pp Mon-Thu / EUR 80pp Fri-Sun, covering the whole pool and sauna area, a wellness bag (robe, towels, slippers) and a cake buffet 14:30-17:00. Treatments are booked separately: the standout is the Romantic Hay Bath for two with partial-body massage, 50 min, EUR 135 - the local hay cure as a couples treatment. Plain 50-min full-body massage is EUR 75, Deep Relax hot stone EUR 80, and there is a Kids SPA oil massage at EUR 40 if the boys want in.
How to get there: Drive ~5 min to Castelrotto. Dolomiti pool 07:30-20:00, sauna and relax area 12:00-20:00. IMPORTANT: under-14s are barred from the sauna/relax area and the Vitarium alpinum, so this is an adults + Rhys/Jude outing - under-13s only get the 08:00-12:00 morning pool at EUR 5. Weekdays are EUR 15pp cheaper, so Mon Oct 12 - Wed Oct 14 beat the weekend. Reserve ahead: +39 0471 707237 / info@abinea.com
Cost: Day spa EUR 65-80pp · couples hay bath + massage EUR 135 · massages EUR 75-80
